info.name: OAN DA Farmers
info.description: DA Services farmer routes for the My Farmers list, search, profile, holdings, photo, registration and update. Data comes live from the Farmer Registry; the frontend calls only DA Services. Run SSO login first (see 0. Sign in). List farmers stores farmer_id and internal_id. List farmers, Farmer details (registry) and Farmer land details (registry) read the Farmer Registry directly with the caller's token; their saved responses are shortened live responses from the dev registry, 25 Nov 2026. The other saved responses are from 31 Oct - 1 Nov 2026. Guide: docs/farmer-frontend-integration.md.

item.name: 0. Sign in
item.description:
Every request sends Authorization: Bearer {{access_token}} and, when csrf_token is set, X-CSRF-Token: {{csrf_token}} (collection pre-request script).

DA Services forwards these two headers to the Farmer Registry, so a local Login token is refused there with 'Unknown Issuer'. For the farmer routes run SSO login: it stores the Keycloak staff access token and its CSRF value. Login and Refresh still work for routes that do not call the registry, such as Who am I.

request.description: Local DA Services login. Stores access_token and refresh_token. Field names are usr and pwd (username / password give 400). Leave usr and pwd in the environment.

Keycloak login through OAN IAM in one call. Stores access_token and csrf_token; the collection then sends both on every request. Set usr, pwd and sso_key in the environment (sso_key is the login key of the user's role, for example agent). Use this on a deployed server, or whenever a route calls a registry.
The access token lasts 15 minutes. Keep the new refresh_token this returns.
Role, role label, the menu paths that role may open, and its scope.

exec: pm.test("Who am I returns 200", function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

query.description: empty = every farmer; or a name, Farmer-ID or phone

request.description: One page of the Farmer Registry register (search_in_a_register), with the caller's own token. filter_by is optional; its region / zone / woreda / kebele keys are filled from the caller's User Permissions, so a DA gets the farmers of their Kebele and a Supervisor those of their Woreda. data is the registry's rows with their own keys and meta its paging. Stores farmer_id (Farmer-ID) and internal_id (internal_record_id) from the first row.

exec: pm.test("List farmers (My Farmers) returns 200", function () { pm.response.to.have.status(200); });

request.description: The farmer's land records straight from the Farmer Registry (get_tab_records of the Lands tab), with the caller's own token. {internal_id} is the internal_record_id of a list row. data is the registry's tab data: the section with is_list false is the farmer's own row, the section with is_list true holds one record per plot (the saved response is shortened). OWNER, SF_HIGH and GRAZING are registry codes; show readable labels. A farmer without land has no plot records.

request.description: Saves every section into one registry draft, then sends it for approval. Returns submission_id and status PENDING_APPROVAL. Use a new client_op_id per registration; a repeat returns DUPLICATE. The FR- id exists only after a supervisor approves. Codes come from Field options and Places.
DRAFT / PENDING_APPROVAL / APPROVED / REJECTED, and the application reference.
DA only, on farmers the DA may edit. Queued, then sent to the registry as a change request. Identity fields cannot change.
Updates not yet in the registry.
